title: Five Out Of Seven
description: A busy customs desk fields a whole batch of uploads at once, some good and some bad, interleaved in no particular order. The database's final tally should match reality exactly, regardless of the mix.
successCondition: For one shipment, upload 7 documents in this exact interleaved order: valid, valid, invalid-mime, valid, oversized (over 5MB), valid, valid. Five uploads succeed (201), two are rejected (400 VALIDATION_ERROR) — confirm the 5/2 split matches. GET /api/booking/:id/documents returns exactly 5 documents. Querying customs_documents via `npm run db:psql` (select count(*) from customs_documents where shipment_id = '<id>') confirms exactly 5 rows, and cross-check each returned document's sizeBytes against the specific valid file it corresponds to, confirming none of the 5 accidentally stored one of the rejected files' bytes.
hints: Building a >5MB file is easy with a script that writes 5*1024*1024 + 1 arbitrary bytes with a valid PDF/JPEG/PNG extension and MIME type — the size check, not the MIME check, is what rejects it.
Track which of your 7 source files is which (by a marker byte sequence or distinct size) so you can confidently match each surviving DB row back to a specific valid upload.
